examples: Para la calle de Calvo Sotelo, un ultraderechista consumado, propondríamos el nombre de algo diametralmente diferente, algo que evoque la participación, la espontaneidad y la voz del pueblo.

entries.etymology: Borrowed from Latin īnfōrmātiōnem (“formation, conception; education”), from the participle stem of īnformāre (“to inform”).

entries.etymology: Inherited from Latin secundus with, per Coromines, a 'semi-learned' treatment of the stressed vowel (*segondo would have been expected otherwise).

entries.etymology: From maravilla + -oso.

entries.etymology: From responder, corrupted by puesta, feminine past participle of poner.

senses.gloss: control, or running of a business

Estoy muy impresionado con su control de calidad.

entries.etymology: Borrowed from French contrôle.

entries.etymology: Inherited from Old Spanish soler (“to use to”), from Latin solēre.

entries.etymology: Borrowed from Latin clientem, based on clueō (“to be called, to be named, to be esteemed”).

senses.gloss: to result, to turn out, to end up, to prove

Te haremos saber el resultado en una semana.

entries.etymology: From Latin resultāre.

Es bastante difícil dominar el francés en 2, 3 años.

entries.etymology: From bastar (“to suffice, be enough”) + -ante.

entries.etymology: Borrowed from Latin systēma, from Ancient Greek σύστημα (sústēma, “organized whole, body”), from σύν (sún, “with, together”) + ἵστημι (hístēmi, “to stand”).

senses.gloss: pitch, (US) field (field on which soccer, rugby or field hockey is played)

entries.etymology: Semi-learned borrowing from Latin cantiōnem f (accusative singular), modified from the original Old Spanish cançón f, which was directly inherited, based on -ción.

entries.etymology: Borrowed from Latin obtinēre, with conjugation based on tener.

entries.etymology: Inherited from Old Spanish lleno, lenno, inherited from Latin plēnus, whence also Spanish pleno, which is a borrowed doublet.

entries.etymology: Borrowed from Latin phantasticus, from Ancient Greek φανταστικός (phantastikós).

A gang of three robbed the bank in broad daylight.
Una banda dirigió la marcha por la ciudad.
A band led the parade through the city.
Los componentes de la banda eran todos ucranianos.
All the members of the band were Ukrainian.
entries.etymology: Borrowed from French bande (“ribbon; group, gang”).

You have changed so much that I can hardly recognize you.
Si lo hubiera sabido, habría cambiado mi plan.
If I had known about it, I would have changed my plan.
Japón ha cambiado mucho en los últimos 50 años.
Japan has changed significantly in the past 50 years.
entries.etymology: Past participle of cambiar.

No me importa hacer las tareas del hogar.

There's a slight possibility of a recurrence.

We have little chance of winning.
Él ha estudiado la posibilidad de una colaboración.
He has studied the possibility of a collaboration.
entries.etymology: Borrowed from Latin possibilitātem, equivalent to posible + -idad.

senses.gloss: to bear, to endure, to withstand, put up with, tolerate, to stomach, to weather, to handle
to support a weight or load

No sé cuántos van a soportar esta situación.
I don't know how many are going to endure this situation.
No puedo soportar ser molestado en el trabajo.
I can't stand being disturbed in my work.
entries.etymology: Borrowed from Latin supportāre.

examples: ¿No sabrás por casualidad cuál es su nombre?
Do you happen to know his name?
Su nombre es conocido por todos en nuestro pueblo.
His name is known to everyone in our town.
Su nombre es conocido en todo el país.
His name is known all over the country.
entries.etymology: Inherited from Old Spanish nombrar, from Latin nōmināre.

examples: El juez le sentenció a cinco años de cárcel.
The judge sentenced him to a jail term of five years.
El juez le condenó a cinco años de prisión.
The judge sentenced him to a jail term of five years.
El reo fue declarado culpable por el juez.
The prisoner was found guilty by the judge.
entries.etymology: Inherited from Old Spanish juez, juiz, judez, from Latin iūdicem.

examples: Fauci señaló que “hay un sentimiento general de anticiencia, antiautoridad y antivacuna entre algunas personas en este país; un porcentaje alarmantemente alto de personas, relativamente hablando”.
“Estos comentarios tan preocupantes están imbuidos de sentimientos de que se tiene cierto derecho sexual, en los que los inceles puntúan más alto que los varones no inceles”.

Love is a feeling that you feel when you feel that you feel a feeling that you have never felt.
Sus sentimientos por él fueron recíprocos.
Her feeling for him was reciprocated.
entries.etymology: From Latin sentimentum; equivalent to sentir + -miento.

examples: La vida no es una ciencia exacta, es un arte.
Life is not an exact science, it is an art.
Preferiría ir al museo de arte que ir al cine.
I would rather go to the art museum than to the movie theater.
Nunca confundas el arte con la vida.
entries.etymology: Borrowed from Latin artem (“practical skill”).

examples: Monſ. Ducan, Dotor de Mompeller, refiere de otro famoſo Medico Francès, que recetaba el Caphè vniverſalmente à todos ſus enfermos.
Mr. Ducan, doctor of Montpellier, refers to another famous French doctor, who prescribed coffee to all of his patiens altogether.
Mi padre toma un café todas las mañanas.
My father drinks a cup of coffee every morning.
El presidente y su secretaria hablaron tomando café.
The president and the secretary talked over a cup of coffee.
Me gustaría tomar una taza de café.
I would like to have a cup of coffee.
entries.etymology: Borrowed from French café, or less likely directly from Italian caffè.

examples: La reina Liliuokalani fue forzada a rendirse.
Queen Liliuokalani was forced to surrender.
En Gran Bretaña el rey reina pero no gobierna.
In Great Britain the king reigns, but does not govern.
En cada colmena sólo puede haber una reina.
In each beehive there can only be one queen.
entries.etymology: Inherited from Old Spanish reyna, with an unexpected shift in stress from [reˈi.na] to [ˈrei̯.na], from Latin rēgīna (“queen”).

examples: Casi todos los japoneses tienen cabello oscuro.
Nearly all Japanese have dark hair.
Los gatos pueden ver cuando está oscuro.
Cats can see in the dark.
El cielo se puso cada vez más oscuro.
The sky became darker and darker.
entries.etymology: Inherited from Old Spanish escuro, with influence from its etymon Latin obscūrus during the Golden Age.

examples: No lo puedo demostrar, pero estoy seguro de que le asesinaron.
I can't prove it, but I'm sure he was murdered.
No lo puedo demostrar, pero estoy seguro de que fue asesinado.
I can't prove it, but I'm sure he was murdered.
entries.etymology: Inherited from Latin dēmōnstrāre.

examples: La muerte es el destino de todas las personas.
Death is the fate of all people.
Nuestro destino depende de vuestras decisiones.
Our fate depends on your decisions.
Nuestro destino depende de nuestras decisiones.
Our destiny depends on our decisions.
entries.etymology: Deverbal from destinar, borrowed from Latin dēstināre.

senses.gloss: to hurt (to cause physical or emotional pain)
to grieve, regret something; to feel sorry about
examples: Me duelo de no haberte llamado cuando estabas enferma.

Le dolía la cabeza pero no se dolió de ello.
His head hurt but he didn't complain about it.
You have a temperature and your throat hurts?
Me duela la muela del juicio.
entries.etymology: Inherited from Old Spanish doler, inherited from Latin dolēre, doleō, from Proto-Italic *doleō (“hurt, cause pain”), from Proto-Indo-European *dolh₁éyeti (“divide”), from *delh₁- (“cut”).

examples: I don't know for what reason
Los motivos fundamentales por los que se ha degradado el arrecife en estos momentos son las mareas rojas y las extracciones de coral por parte de los humanos.

What is the reason for that lie?
¿Cuál es el motivo de su visita?
What is the purpose of your visit?
El profesor le echó la bronca al alumno sin motivo alguno.
The teacher scolded the student for no reason.
entries.etymology: Borrowed from Late Latin motīvus.

examples: La estrella no tenía más remedio que retirarse después de una conmoción grave.
The star had no choice but to retire after a really bad concussion.
Si necesitas dinero lo puedes retirar del banco.
You can withdraw some money out of the bank, if you need any.
Usted se puede retirar ahora, caballero.
Tengo que retirar dinero del banco.
I have to withdraw some cash from the bank.
entries.etymology: From re- + tirar.

senses.gloss: operation (the method or practice by which actions are done)
operation (a procedure for generating a value from one or more other values)

examples: ¿El paciente está preparado para la operación?
Is the patient prepared for surgery?
Mi padre se ha sentido bien desde la operación.
My father has been in good shape since his operation.
La operación viola la ley internacional.
entries.etymology: Borrowed from Latin operātiōnem.

examples: no estar en su sano juicio
not be in one's right mind
El exdirectivo de RTVV afirmó tener ganas de que se celebrara el juicio para poder "restablecer" su honor.

El ladrón acusado ahora está en un juicio.
The accused thief is on trial now.
Le sacaron las muelas del juicio a Brian.
Brian got his wisdom teeth out.
Me están saliendo las muelas del juicio.
My wisdom teeth are coming in.
entries.etymology: Inherited from Old Spanish judizio, juyzio, borrowed from Latin iūdicium (“judgement, decision”) (compare Italian giudizio, Portuguese juízo).

Don't laugh at him for making a mistake.
Él tiene miedo de cometer algún error.

entries.etymology: Inherited from Old Spanish cometer, from Latin committere.

examples: Es más fácil pedir perdón que obtener permiso.

Perdón, ¿sabe cuál es el pronóstico para mañana?

Perdón por llegar tarde: me quedé dormido.

entries.etymology: Deverbal from perdonar.

Mi cabello es igual de largo que el de Jane.

Whatever you say, I'll do it my way.
Tom no es igual de perseverante que Bill.
Tom is no more hardworking than Bill is.
entries.etymology: Inherited from Old Spanish igual~egual (both common in the 13th century), from Latin aequālis.

entries.etymology: From Latin investīgāre.

examples: ¿Qué diablos estás haciendo en mi cuarto?

What the hell are you doing with my gun?
¿De qué diablos quieres hablar con Tom?
What on earth do you want to talk to Tom about?
entries.etymology: Plural form of diablo (“devil”).

examples: Un capitán está por sobre un sargento.

He rose to the rank of sergeant.

The father had met the sergeant last year.
entries.etymology: Inherited from Old Spanish sargente, from Middle French sergent, from Old French sergeant, sergent, serjant, sergient, sergant (“sergeant, servant”), from Medieval Latin servientem (“servant, vassal, soldier, apparitor”), from Latin serviēns (“serving”), present participle of serviō (“to serve or to be a slave to”), from servus (“a slave, a serf or a servant”), perhaps from Etruscan; compare Etruscan proper names 𐌔𐌄𐌓𐌅𐌉 (servi) or 𐌔𐌄𐌓𐌅𐌄 (serve); or from Proto-Italic *serwo, from Proto-Indo-European *serwoh₂.

¿Cuánto tiempo se tarda en llegar a la estación?

A cubic meter corresponds to 1000 liters.
entries.etymology: Borrowed from French mètre, from Ancient Greek μέτρον (métron, “measure”).

¡Sería genial si pudiera hablar diez idiomas!

La primera edición se publicó hace diez años.

La calle estaba desierta después de las diez.

entries.etymology: Borrowed from Latin exitus (“exit, conclusion, result”), perfect passive participle of exeō (“to go out”).

entries.etymology: Inherited from Late Latin bassus.

entries.etymology: Borrowed from Latin experientia (“knowledge; experience”).

My dog can understand Esperanto but can't speak it.
entries.etymology: Feminine of perro (“dog”).

senses.gloss: to find oneself in a certain way (+adjective)

I finally found a use for this old thing.
Tom fue hallado muerto en su habitación.

entries.etymology: Borrowed from Old Catalan relotge (1362) (Modern Catalan rellotge), from the older orollotge, from Latin hōrologium, from Ancient Greek ὡρολόγιον (hōrológion).
relatedWords: en el sentido de las agujas del reloj
en sentido contrario a las agujas del reloj

senses.gloss: cinema; A sophisticated or exemplary film, representative of the art of cinema.
Any media or event that is exemplary.
examples: es que es cine, enamorado me encuentro de ella, si me veo oshi no ko es por ella
I mean it is cinema, I'm in love with her, if I'm watching Oshi no Ko is because of her
Preferiría ir al museo de arte que ir al cine.
I would rather go to the art museum than to the movie theater.
Generalmente yo iba al cine los domingos.
I usually went to the movies on Sunday.
Este es el cine donde vemos películas extranjeras.
This is the theater where we see foreign movies.
entries.etymology: Clipping of cinema, from Ancient Greek κῑ́νημα (kī́nēma, “movement”).

senses.gloss: to crash or break down (a computer)
to rule, give (a verdict or sentence)

examples: Si vas a esa velocidad, seguramente vas a fallar.
If you go on at that rate, you will surely fail.
Un plan así está destinado a fallar.
Such a plan is bound to fail.
Si todo lo demás falla, reinicia el sistema.
If all else fails, reboot the system.
entries.etymology: From falla, of Catalan origin, ultimately from Latin fallere and hence cognate with English fail.

senses.gloss: memory (the ability of the brain to record information)
memory (a specific thing that is remembered)
memory (the part of a computer that stores variable executable code or data)
examples: Necesitarías 3 millones 809.280 memorias flash de un gigabyte para almacenar todas esas fotos. […] Necesitarías cuando menos 238,080 iPhones S6 con 16 gigabytes de memoria para guardarlas.
Si mi memoria es correcta, ellos son primos.
They are cousins, if I remember rightly.
Los mentirosos tienen que tener buena memoria.
Liars must have a good memory.
La sala fue construida en memoria del fundador.
The hall was built in memory of the founder.
entries.etymology: Inherited from Old Spanish memoria (“memory”), from Latin memoria.

examples: Tenía la intención de haberte visitado ayer.
I had intended to visit you yesterday.
El hombre la atacó con intención de matarla.
The man attacked her with the intention of killing her.
No es su intención ser malo. Es su naturaleza.
He doesn't mean to be mean. It's just his nature.
entries.etymology: Borrowed from Latin intentiōnem.
relatedWords: el infierno está empedrado de buenas intenciones

senses.gloss: absolutely; completely; entirely; totally; utterly; wholly (in absolute manner)

examples: No sé absolutamente nada acerca de ese plan.
I know absolutely nothing about that plan.
No comí absolutamente nada en todo el día.
I ate absolutely nothing the whole day.
No entiendo absolutamente nada de alemán.
I don't understand German at all.
entries.etymology: From absoluto + -mente.

senses.gloss: politics (activities associated with running a government or organisation)
policy (a formal principle or protocol of conduct)

examples: La ley y la política son dos cosas diferentes.
Law and politics are two different things.
La honestidad no es siempre la mejor política.
Honesty is not always the best policy.
Estamos hartos de la corrupción política.
We are sick and tired of political corruption.
El agua transmite mejor el sonido que el aire.
Water transmits sound better than air.
El aire de las grandes ciudades está contaminado.
entries.etymology: Inherited from Old Spanish aire, ayre, from Latin āēr, from Ancient Greek ἀήρ (aḗr).

senses.gloss: French (as in French food, clothing, etc.)

examples: Ella habla alemán y francés, además de inglés.
She speaks German and French, not to mention English.
I don't speak French well enough!
Además de inglés, él puede hablar francés.
In addition to English, he can speak French.
entries.etymology: Inherited from Latin francēnsis.

examples: Él siempre está dispuesto a ayudar a los demás.
He is always willing to help others.
Él estaba dispuesto a trabajar para otros.
He was willing to work for others.
Yo estoy dispuesto a admitir su petición.
I am willing to agree to your request.
entries.etymology: From the verb disponer.

senses.gloss: exhibition (artistic or technological collection for display)
sign, token, display (e.g. of gratitude, of respect, of love)

examples: Esta es una muestra gratis. No cuesta nada.
This is a free sample. It doesn't cost anything.
Ella no muestra entusiasmo por su trabajo.
She shows no zeal for her work.
Me tomaron una muestra de sangre en el hospital.
They took a sample of my blood at the hospital.
entries.etymology: Deverbal from mostrar.

examples: Me dijo una dirección equivocada a propósito.
She told me a wrong address on purpose.
Yo he herido sus sentimientos a propósito.
I hurt her feelings on purpose.
¿Crees que cometió ese error a propósito?
Do you think he made that mistake on purpose?
entries.etymology: Borrowed from Latin prōpositum (“that which is proposed”).

examples: Como iba con prisa, tuve que tomar un taxi.
As I was in a hurry, I had to take a taxi.
Es difícil conseguir un taxi fuera de la estación.
It's hard to get a taxi outside the station.
Tomé un taxi porque estaba lloviendo.
I took a taxi because it was raining.
entries.etymology: Clipping of taxímetro.

examples: Ataron los brazos y las piernas del prisionero.
They bound the prisoner's arms and legs.
Mis piernas son más pequeñas que las tuyas.
My legs are smaller than yours.
Algunos hombres se afeitan las piernas.
Él lucía como si hubiera visto a un fantasma.
He looked as if he had seen a ghost.
Asegura apagar todas las luces antes de salir.
Make sure to turn off all the lights before going out.
Ella lucía como si hubiera visto a un fantasma.
She looked as if she had seen a ghost.
entries.etymology: Inherited from Vulgar Latin *lūcīre, from Latin lūcēre.

senses.gloss: to yield, pay, submit, pass down
to surrender, give in, give up
examples: rendirse a los pies de alguien

senses.gloss: to take a test or an exam

examples: You're never going to give in, are you?
Se le pidió que rindiera cuentas de su conducta.
She was asked to account for her conduct.
Si estuviera en su lugar, todavía no me rendiría.
If I were in her place, I wouldn't give up yet.
entries.etymology: Inherited from Old Spanish rendir, older render, from Late Latin rendere, from Latin reddere.

examples: Este medicamento debe ser tomado cada tres horas.
This medicine should be taken every three hours.
Me temo que he tomado un tren equivocado.
I'm afraid I have taken a wrong train.
Te has tomado mucho tiempo para almorzar.
You've taken a long time eating lunch.
entries.etymology: Past participle of tomar.

examples: No hay lugar a dudas de que él fue asesinado.
There is no doubt that he was murdered.
Julio César, el gran héroe romano, fue asesinado.
Julius Caesar, this great Roman hero, was assassinated.
El soldado fue asesinado en combate.
The soldier was killed in action.
Dices algo y luego haces justo lo contrario.
You say one thing and then act just the opposite.
Mary no es pobre. Al contrario, es bastante rica.
Mary is not poor. On the contrary, she is quite rich.
Tú eres joven. Yo, por el contrario, soy muy viejo.
You are young. I, on the contrary, am very old.
entries.etymology: From Latin contrārius.
relatedWords: en sentido contrario a las agujas del reloj

examples: "¿Qué marca es tu coche?" "Es un Ford."
"What brand is your car?" "It's a Ford."
¿De qué color y de qué marca es el coche del director?
What brand and what color is the director's car?
¿Cuál es tu marca de jabón favorita?
What's your favorite brand of soap?
entries.etymology: Inherited from Late Latin marca, of Germanic origin, related to Old High German marka and Old Norse mark.

senses.gloss: to be lacking, to lack, to not have (of a quality or circumstance)
to be lacking, to lack, to not have (of a person)

examples: Falta un mes para mi cumpleaños.
My birthday is a month away.

senses.gloss: to be absent, to be missing

examples: Para ser perfecta sólo le faltaba un defecto.
To be perfect she lacked just one defect.
Debido a la falta de evidencias claras, el prisionero fue dejado en libertad.
In the absence of firm evidence the prisoner was set free.
Puede que Luciano tenga gran apoyo popular, pero todavía le falta experiencia.
Luciano might have the crowd behind him, but he's still wet behind the ears.
entries.etymology: Inherited from Old Spanish faltar (“to lack”).
relatedWords: faltar el canto de un duro

senses.gloss: to pretend (to act as though something is different from what it is)

examples: Vamos a fingir que somos alienígenas.
No puedo fingir que me gusta.
I can't pretend to like him.
Él ocultó sus emociones y fingía entusiasmo.
He hid his emotions and pretended enthusiasm.
entries.etymology: Borrowed from Latin fingere.

examples: Yo estaba encantado con el rendimiento del grupo.
I was enchanted by the performance of the group.
My name's Cyril; pleased to meet you!
"The castle is haunted," he said with a shiver.
Comparado con mi problema, el tuyo no es nada.
As compared with my trouble, yours is nothing.
El mío no es tan bueno como el tuyo.
Mine is not so good as yours.
Mi reloj es menos caro que el tuyo.
My watch is less expensive than yours.
entries.etymology: From tu, modified by analogy with cuyo.

senses.gloss: paroxytone; stressed in the penultimate syllable

examples: No te pongas así. No es tan grave como parece.
Don't be like that. It's not as bad as it looks.
Cometí un grave error al elegir a mi esposa.
I made a big mistake when choosing my wife.
El niño luchaba contra una grave enfermedad.
The boy battled against a serious illness.
entries.etymology: Inherited from Old Spanish grave, from Latin gravis.

examples: La fe es creer en lo que sabes que no es cierto.
Faith is believing what you know ain't true.
La fe nunca es perfecta, pero el conocimiento sí.
Faith is never perfect, but knowledge is.
La fe es la muerte de la inteligencia.
Belief is the death of intelligence.
entries.etymology: Inherited from Old Spanish fe, fee, from Latin fidēs, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *bʰeydʰ- (“to command, to persuade, to trust”).

senses.gloss: to acknowledge (to notify sender of having received)
to show; to show signs of
examples: se acusa una notoria escasez de información
A clear lack of information is shown
La compañía alemana acusa el fin del auge del comercio electrónico y los beneficios se hunden un 92% en 2022[.]
The German company is facing the end of the e-commerce boom and profits plunge 92% in 2022[.]

senses.gloss: to snitch, tattle, rat, egg, squeal

examples: No lo puedes acusar de haber robado a menos que tengas pruebas.
You can't accuse him of stealing unless you have proof.
Me acusaron de no haber cumplido mi promesa.
They accused me of having broken my promise.
Los dos hombres se acusaron el uno al otro.
The two men accused each other.
entries.etymology: Inherited from Old Spanish acusar, from Latin accūsāre.

examples: No me sentía con confianza de poder hacer eso.
I was uncertain of my ability to do it.
Él ganó nuestra confianza con su honestidad.
He won us over with his honesty.
La sociedad se construye sobre la confianza.
entries.etymology: From confiar + -anza.

senses.gloss: shot; gunshot (the result of launching a projectile or bullet)
range (the distance from a person or sensor to an object)
shooting (the sport or activity of firing a gun or other weapon)
shot (the act of launching a ball or similar object toward a goal)
intake of air in a space
inseam (the seam of a trouser up the inside of the leg)

examples: Dio al centro del blanco con su primer tiro.
He hit the center of the target with his first shot.
«Alguien se tiró un pedo.» «¡No fui yo!»
Alguien se tiró un pedo en el ascensor.
entries.etymology: Deverbal from tirar (“to throw”).
relatedWords: matar dos pájaros de un tiro
no van por ahí los tiros
salir el tiro por la culata

examples: El policía culpó al taxista por el accidente.
The policeman blamed the taxi driver for the accident.
No te culpo por el accidente. No fue culpa tuya.
I don't blame you for the accident. It wasn't your fault.
Él me convenció de que no era su culpa.
He convinced me that it was not his fault.
entries.etymology: Borrowed from Latin culpāre.

examples: ¿Hay alguna evidencia que apoye esta postura?
Is there any evidence that supports his position?
Este coche pondrá a otros coches en evidencia.
This new car will put other cars to shame.
La evidencia nos convenció de su inocencia.
The evidence convinced us of his innocence.
entries.etymology: Borrowed from Latin ēvidentia.

examples: Ha salido al aeropuerto a despedir a un amigo.
He went to the airport to see his friend off.
Si alguien viene a verme dile que he salido.
If anyone comes to see me, tell him that I am out.
Casi no han salido desde que nació el bebé.
They have scarcely gone out since the baby was born.
entries.etymology: Past participle of salir.

examples: Necesitamos un cuchillo para la mantequilla.
We need a knife for the butter.
Eso no es un cuchillo. ESTO es un cuchillo.
That's not a knife. THIS is a knife.
No dejes al niño jugar con el cuchillo.
Don't let the kid play with the knife.
entries.etymology: Inherited from Old Spanish cuchiello, from Latin cultellus, a diminutive of culter.
relatedWords: en casa de herrero, cuchillo de palo

examples: He loves it when you smile at him.
La niña no le sonríe a nadie mas que a Emily.
The little girl never smiles at anyone other than Emily.
Las dos muchachas jóvenes sonrieron felizmente.
The two young girls smiled happily.
Todos los que salen en la foto están sonriendo.
Everybody in the picture is smiling.
entries.etymology: Inherited from Old Spanish sonreir, from Vulgar Latin *subrīdīre, from Latin subrīdēre.
